segments.title: 第24章 送雨傘
segments.content:
Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 24: Delivering an Umbrella

Fortunately, it was just a light cut on the skin, nothing too serious.

Li Luo, with much familiarity, found a small first-aid kit in one of Ying Chanxi's cabinets. He dipped a cotton swab in some iodophor and disinfected the cut for Ying Zhicheng.

Then he covered it with a band-aid, and that was pretty much it. However, if he were to cook now, his finger would definitely hurt a bit.

"Uncle Ying."

"Hm?"

"It's not convenient for you to cook with that hand. Why don't you let me?"

"Ah?" Ying Zhicheng frowned, trying to hold the knife himself. He gestured a few times with his left hand, but it still hurt a little. "Can you handle it?"

He had only cooked for a period of time after his wife passed away, when he was home taking care of Ying Chanxi.

After his work became completely busy, he never touched the kitchen again.

But even so, he was still a bit more reliable than a kid like Li Luo.

"Trust me, no problem." Li Luo patted his chest in assurance. "My family runs a breakfast shop, after all. I've learned a thing or two from my dad."

Hearing Li Luo say this, Ying Zhicheng hesitated slightly.

But thinking of Li Luo's grades that got him into Fuyi High, and his various attitudes and ways of handling things since they met today, Ying Zhicheng finally nodded. "Then you can give it a try. If it doesn't work out, I'll take over."

"Alright."

Li Luo accepted the task, glanced at the ingredients Ying Zhicheng had prepared, picked up the kitchen knife, and sliced half of the remaining pork belly, and shredded the other half.

The knife thudded against the cutting board with a rapid, crisp, and clean rhythm, making Ying Zhicheng raise his eyebrows.

You call this learning a thing or two?

Just this skill in chopping vegetables was not something a beginner could pull off.

After prepping the ingredients, Li Luo glanced at the chicken soup Ying Zhicheng had been simmering earlier, ladled out a bowl for later use, perfect for stir-frying to enhance the flavor.

Then, Ying Zhicheng felt as if Li Luo had transformed.

Dish after dish of ingredients were poured into the wok with precision. After being stir-fried by Li Luo, the kitchen was instantly filled with a rich aroma.

To be honest, seeing this skilled display, Ying Zhicheng felt that even if the taste was just average, it would definitely be much better than his own cooking.

"When did you learn to cook?" Although Ying Zhicheng's finger was injured, helping to carry a plate now and then was no problem. As he helped, he couldn't help but ask.

"I've been helping at the shop every day recently, you just pick it up by watching," Li Luo fibbed. "Uncle Ying, it's rare for you to come back. If you want to give Ying Chanxi a surprise, then you're the one who cooked tonight's meal."

"How could I take credit for that?"

"Uncle, don't be so formal. I come over to play on your computer every day. What's cooking a meal?" Li Luo said while stir-frying. "Besides, this wasn't your fault. Your finger is injured, so the thought is what counts."

Hearing him say that, Ying Zhicheng didn't say anything more, which was taken as a silent agreement.

By the time all the dishes were on the table, it was already past five in the evening.

Li Luo had prepared a table full of food, a feast for the eyes, nose, and palate, just waiting for the person to arrive.

At that moment, Li Luo's phone rang.

He washed his hands, wiped them vigorously on his apron, then took out his phone and saw it was a call from Ying Chanxi.

He gestured to Ying Zhicheng and answered the call.

"Hello? What's up?"

"Li Luo, where are you right now?" Ying Chanxi asked in a low voice.

"At your place," Li Luo said. "What's wrong now? I've already put your clothes in your bedroom."

"Oh, oh, thanks," Ying Chanxi said. "But I didn't bring an umbrella when I went out today. I got on the bus with a classmate, but we don't get off at the same stop. Can you come pick me up at the bus stop?"

"Sure. How long until you arrive?"

"About ten minutes."

"OK, see you in a bit."

After hanging up, Li Luo looked at Ying Zhicheng.

Ying Zhicheng nodded at him. "Go ahead and pick her up. I'll clean up the kitchen."

"Okay, I'm heading out then."

Li Luo walked out of the kitchen, changed his shoes, took his own umbrella from by the door, and also grabbed Ying Chanxi's.

Then he went out, opened his umbrella, and walked into the rain toward the nearest bus stop.

...

On the bus.

Liu Shaowen sat in the third row, staring at the driver's rearview mirror. He had been looking for several minutes.

Ying Chanxi was sitting in the seat near the rear door of the bus, clearly visible in the rearview mirror.

As the long-standing second-place student in Yucai Middle School, Liu Shaowen had always held a special feeling in his heart for the figure of that first-place student.

He was the number one in the honors class, while Ying Chanxi was the number one in the parallel class.

Although they didn't interact much at school, only chatting a bit when participating in competitions.

But in Liu Shaowen's inner world, he felt he had long since connected with Ying Chanxi on a spiritual level.

After all, in the vast Yucai Middle School, he was the only one who could keep up with her pace.

Especially when it came to the independent admissions for Fuyi High.

Twenty-seven students from the whole school successfully got into Fuyi High, but among the top forty, there were only Shaowen and Chanxi.

Fuyi High's summer preparatory program was directly divided into four classes based on grades.

Liu Shaowen and Ying Chanxi were naturally placed in Class One.

It had to be said, there was a kind of fate tangling them together in the unseen.

Liu Shaowen was quite tall and had pleasant features. Apart from slightly darker skin and wearing glasses, he had no other flaws.

Back in Yucai Middle School, he had secretly received quite a few love letters from girls.

However, because the white moonlight already resided in his heart, Liu Shaowen simply ignored them all.

But he would often inquire about how many love letters Ying Chanxi had recently received.

If the number was about the same as his, Liu Shaowen would feel a sense of serene contentment, as if this was the fate between them.

There were many similar incidents.

For example, every Monday, the school would invite outstanding student representatives to speak on stage.

Over the three years, he and Ying Chanxi were the ones scheduled to speak most often.

And when it came to various school awards, their two names were often indispensable.

After the monthly exams, as well as the mid-term and final exams, the bulletin board posting the school-wide rankings was Liu Shaowen's favorite place to go.

Because there, he was always suppressed by Ying Chanxi, unable to turn the tables.

But no one else could take away his second-place position either.

Now, in Fuyi High's summer preparatory program, within Class One, only he and Ying Chanxi were from Yucai Middle School.

This gave rise to a special bond within him, as if he had taken on the attribute of some kind of guardian knight, always wanting to do something for Ying Chanxi.

Just like today's heavy rain.

He noticed that Ying Chanxi didn't bring an umbrella.

So when school let out in the evening, he deliberately packed his bag early, went downstairs to the path Ying Chanxi had to take to leave school, and waited quietly while holding his umbrella.

In his fantasy, Ying Chanxi would arrive at the teaching building exit, raise a hand to shield her head, gaze at the dense curtain of rain before her, and perhaps a cute, troubled expression would appear on her face.

At that moment, he would be standing nearby, seemingly having unintentionally caught a glimpse of her vexed expression, and would then ask in a very casual tone, "Are you taking the bus home?"

Having struck up a conversation like that, he would follow with a light chuckle, "It's on my way. Let me walk you."

The fantasy was beautiful, and Liu Shaowen waited at the exit of the teaching building just as he had imagined.

But Ying Chanxi didn't come out alone; her new deskmate was with her.

The two of them walked into the rain under an umbrella, heading towards the bus stop.

But it didn't matter.

Liu Shaowen dodged his dad who had come to pick him up, followed them onto the bus, and found a seat in the front.

That female deskmate probably didn't get off at the same stop as Ying Chanxi, so he still had a chance.

When the time came, he could pretend to be a classmate getting off at the same stop and then conveniently walk her home under his umbrella.

At this thought, Liu Shaowen's spirits lifted, and his body trembled slightly with excitement.

At this moment, the bus stopped at a station.

An old grandmother got on through the front door.

By this time, the bus had completed more than half of its route, and all the seats were taken.

Seeing the old grandmother holding onto the handrail as she stood, Liu Shaowen immediately looked towards Ying Chanxi in the back.

Then, he stood up resolutely and said to the old lady, "Grandma, you can sit here."

"No, no." The old lady politely declined. "You sit, you sit."

"It's alright," Liu Shaowen said with a smile. "I'm getting off soon anyway. Please, Grandma, have a seat."

Since Liu Shaowen insisted, the old lady immediately thanked him and sat down in his seat.

Then, Liu Shaowen puffed out his chest and walked to the handrail by the rear door to stand.

Although he didn't look in Ying Chanxi's direction, he could guess that at this very moment, Ying Chanxi was probably looking at him.

And with a gaze of admiration and praise.

At this thought, Liu Shaowen's posture became even more upright, as if the zipper on his school uniform over his chest was about to burst.

The bus then passed two more stops before slowly turning onto Ou Hua Zhou Avenue and stopping in front of the bus station.

Liu Shaowen saw Ying Chanxi stand up and instantly came to his senses, realizing she was about to get off.

Once the bus stopped steadily and the rear door opened, Liu Shaowen took the first step, got off the bus, opened his umbrella, and waited inside the bus shelter.

He thought.

When Ying Chanxi gets off the bus and sees how heavy the rain is, he could naturally offer to walk her home under his umbrella.

"Huh?" Inside the bus stop, after opening his umbrella, Liu Shaowen turned around at the perfect moment, looked at Ying Chanxi who was getting off the bus, and asked with a surprised expression, "You get off at this stop too?"

"Yeah." Ying Chanxi looked at Liu Shaowen, a hint of confusion on her face as well. "What's wrong?"

Because this was the first time in over a month that she had seen Liu Shaowen on the bus.

"You didn't bring an umbrella, did you?" Liu Shaowen smiled faintly, raised the umbrella in his hand, and gestured. "It's raining pretty hard right now. I can walk you. Your home should be nearby, right?"

"Oh, thank you." Ying Chanxi thanked him politely, then shook her head and pointed behind Liu Shaowen. "Someone's here to pick me up."

As soon as she said this, Liu Shaowen was startled.

After all, in his mind, the person who would pick up Ying Chanxi at a bus stop near her home had to be her parent.

Am I going to meet her parents this soon?

Isn't that a bit inappropriate?

With this thought, Liu Shaowen slowly turned around, silently preparing a script in his mind on how to greet them to leave a good impression.

But when he turned around and saw a boy about his age, his expression went blank for a moment.

Li Luo looked at Liu Shaowen with a strange expression, then tossed the umbrella in his hand into Ying Chanxi's arms and said to her, "Let's go, time to go home and eat."

Liu Shaowen looked at Li Luo's face, feeling that it was somewhat familiar.

Then he quickly composed himself and asked Ying Chanxi casually, "Is this your younger brother?"

Ying Chanxi was visibly stunned for a moment, then she chuckled. "Yes, yes."

After speaking, she opened the umbrella Li Luo had brought, walked side by side with him into the rain, not forgetting to turn her head and say to Liu Shaowen, "Thank you for your kind offer. Bye-bye."

Hiss... Liu Shaowen's breath hitched as he watched the girl's back. Although his plan didn't go as he wished, it seemed to have turned out alright.

She said thank you to me...

At that moment, the phone in his pocket vibrated again.

Liu Shaowen hurriedly answered the call.

"Where did you run off to? The teacher said you already left! How did you just disappear? I've been waiting at the school gate for twenty minutes, and you didn't even answer your phone!"

"Dad! I..."

...

On the way home, Li Luo grumbled, "Who's your younger brother?"

"You were born a day after me. If you're not my younger brother, what are you?"

"Who was that just now? He looked a bit familiar."

"Him? A classmate from the prep program. He's from Yucai too, but I don't know him well."
